__inputs.name: DS_CLICKHOUSE
__inputs.label: Cloudflare Analytics Engine
__inputs.description: Altinity ClickHouse datasource pointed at the Cloudflare AE SQL API. Setup: mcp-server/src/docs/operations/GRAFANA.md

title: GST MCP Server
description: Analytics Engine dashboard for the GST MCP server. Panels cover only event types that actually emit in production — see the 'What this dashboard deliberately does not show' panel. Every count uses sum(_sample_interval), not count(), because AE samples.

list.name: dataset
list.label: Dataset
list.description: AE dataset. Production carries the traffic; staging is near-empty by design (no cron, little use).

panels.title: Trial signups over time, by outcome
panels.description: Every branch of POST /trial/signup emits one event. A rising 'unavailable' line means a secret is unbound or Upstash/Turnstile is failing — the failure mode that is otherwise invisible without a live wrangler tail. Live since 2026-09-08. One sumIf column per outcome, NOT a GROUP BY blob4 (BL-158): the Altinity plugin turns extra COLUMNS into series, while an extra grouped ROW per timestamp merges into one line — this panel shipped merged and read as a single series. The column list is exhaustive over OUTCOME_VALUES.trial_signup and a guard test fails if an outcome is added without a column.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'minted')           AS minted,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'reissued')         AS reissued,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'challenge-failed') AS challenge_failed,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'rate-limited')     AS rate_limited,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'expired')          AS expired,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'in-progress')      AS in_progress,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'bad-request')      AS bad_request,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'unavailable')      AS unavailable
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'trial_signup' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Signup outcomes in window
panels.description: The signup-health view. 'minted' and 'reissued' are successes; everything else is a refusal or a fault. Compare 'unavailable' against the rest to read the failure rate.

targets.query:
SELECT blob4 AS outcome, blob6 AS status_code, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'trial_signup' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob4, blob6
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Distinct active trials
panels.description: count(DISTINCT blob8) over trial tool calls. SAMPLING CAVEAT: a DISTINCT count has no sample correction. Cloudflare corrects the plain row counter count() (via sum(_sample_interval)), plus sum/avg/quantile — but count(DISTINCT x) is a different aggregate and is NOT among them, because a distinct-count over rows sampling dropped cannot be recovered by weighting the survivors. So this is EXACT while the dataset is unsampled and a LOWER BOUND once it is not, dropping the quietest talkers first. It under-reports, never over-reports. For an exact count of live trials use GET /admin/oauth/m2m-clients and count tier === 'trial'. See ADR-0031.

targets.query:
SELECT count(DISTINCT blob8) AS distinct_trials
FROM $dataset
WHERE index1 = 'OAUTH:M2M:TRIAL' AND blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter

panels.title: Per-trial call volume (top talkers)
panels.description: The 'is someone farming this' view. Sample-correct: sum(_sample_interval) is the corrected form of count(). blob8 is the per-client dimension (OAUTH:<clientId>) — a blob, never the index, so index1 stays roster-sized (ADR-0031).

targets.query:
SELECT blob8 AS client, sum(_sample_interval) AS calls
FROM $dataset
WHERE index1 = 'OAUTH:M2M:TRIAL' AND blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob8
ORDER BY calls DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Invocations over time, by primitive
panels.description: Tools, Resources and Prompts. The event-type allowlist is explicit rather than a bare GROUP BY blob1, so this panel cannot silently plot event types the dashboard says it omits. One sumIf column per primitive, NOT a GROUP BY blob1 (BL-158) — extra columns become series, extra grouped rows merge into one line.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob1 = 'tool_invocation')   AS tool_invocation,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob1 = 'resource_read')     AS resource_read,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob1 = 'prompt_invocation') AS prompt_invocation
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 IN ('tool_invocation', 'resource_read', 'prompt_invocation') AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Top keyOwners in window
panels.description: index1 is the AE sampling key and is deliberately roster-sized: one value per team key, plus one constant per M2M tier (all trials share OAUTH:M2M:TRIAL). Unauthenticated and cron traffic lands in __none__. A TABLE, not a timeseries, on purpose (BL-158): splitting a timeseries by a column requires one sumIf column per value, and the keyOwner roster grows whenever a key is issued — so any column list here would go stale silently. A table needs no such list and answers the ranking question directly.

targets.query:
SELECT index1 AS key_owner, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 IN ('tool_invocation', 'resource_read', 'prompt_invocation') AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY index1
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 25

SELECT blob2 AS name, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Status codes (events that record one)
panels.description: BL-159: this panel used to read blob1 IN (tool_invocation, resource_read, prompt_invocation) GROUP BY blob6, and could never return a status code — NONE of those three write status_code. Over 863 real invocations it returned exactly one row: the empty string. It now reads the five event types that DO record one (see FIELD_EMITTED_BY in metrics/_schema.ts): inoreader_call, trial_signup, rate_limit_decision (deny only), tier_denial, scope_denial. Grouped by blob1 AS WELL as blob6 on purpose — tier_denial's synthetic '200' would otherwise conflate with a real Inoreader 200, which are not the same fact. blob6 != '' drops rate_limit_decision throttle rows, which carry no status. This is the only panel showing scope 403s.

targets.query:
SELECT blob1 AS event_type, blob6 AS status_code, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 IN ('inoreader_call', 'trial_signup', 'rate_limit_decision', 'tier_denial', 'scope_denial') AND blob6 != '' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob1, blob6
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Refusals over time, by outcome
panels.description: Only REFUSALS are emitted — 'deny' (the window was exhausted, the caller got a 429) and 'throttle' (allowed, but some bucket is >=80% spent). One sumIf column per outcome, NOT a GROUP BY blob4 (BL-158) — extra columns become series, extra grouped rows merge into one line. TWO columns, not three: OUTCOME_VALUES.rate_limit_decision also lists 'allow', and there is deliberately no allow series — emitting one would write a row per authenticated request and push this dataset into sampling, which silently degrades the count(DISTINCT blob8) query on 'Distinct active trials'. See ADR-0032.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'deny')     AS deny,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob4 = 'throttle') AS throttle
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'rate_limit_decision' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Refusals by client and responsible bucket
panels.description: Who is hitting which wall. blob2 is the bucket the operator should act on, filled asymmetrically by design: on 'deny' it is the bucket that refused; on 'throttle' it is the bucket nearest its cliff, which is not necessarily the binding one. That is why this groups by outcome too — reading blob2 alone mixes the two meanings. blob8 is the per-client ref (ADR-0031), empty for static bearer keys, which have no per-client identity.

targets.query:
SELECT blob8 AS client_ref, blob2 AS responsible_bucket, blob4 AS outcome, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'rate_limit_decision' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob8, blob2, blob4
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Trial paywall hits over time
panels.description: A trial identity was refused a radar tool by the tier gate. This is upgrade INTENT, not an error: someone wanted the gated product. Expected empty until the self-serve trial goes live in production — an empty chart here is not a broken query.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'tier_denial' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Which radar tools trials ask for
panels.description: The commercial signal in this dashboard: which gated capability trials reach for, ranked. Read it as a demand curve for the paid tier, not a fault list. Expected empty until trial go-live.

targets.query:
SELECT blob2 AS refused_tool, blob8 AS client_ref, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'tier_denial' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2, blob8
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Upstream I/O wait per tool
panels.description: NOT total handler time, and the title says so because BL-159 found this panel reporting p50/p95/p99 = 0 for search_portfolio across 279 calls — which reads as 'instant' and means 'never measured'. Cloudflare Workers freeze the clock outside I/O (Date.now() returns the time of the last I/O), so duration_ms is time BLOCKED ON I/O and a compute-only tool scores exactly 0 however much work it does. See with-metrics.ts (BL-122). The HAVING clause drops tools with a zero p99, mirroring what /status does at render — p99 and not p50, because a tool that reaches the network only on a cache miss has p50 = 0 and a real p99 and must survive. TRADE: /status keeps the unfiltered rows so it can distinguish 'no invocations at all' from 'traffic existed, none measurable'; filtering in SQL collapses those into one blank panel. If this is empty, check 'Top tools in window' beside it to tell which one you are looking at.

targets.query:
SELECT blob2 AS name,
       quantileWeighted(0.5, double1, _sample_interval) AS p50_ms,
       quantileWeighted(0.95, double1, _sample_interval) AS p95_ms,
       quantileWeighted(0.99, double1, _sample_interval) AS p99_ms,
       sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2
HAVING quantileWeighted(0.99, double1, _sample_interval) > 0
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Outcomes by tool
panels.description: success vs error per tool. A tool appearing only with outcome 'error' is the shape worth chasing.

targets.query:
SELECT blob2 AS name, blob4 AS outcome, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2, blob4
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Zone-1 calls over time, by category
panels.description: blob7 = '1' isolates Zone-1 categories from the OAuth refresh path. This is the Inoreader-funded budget the radar tools draw on, and the reason radar is denied to the trial tier. One sumIf column per category, NOT a GROUP BY blob2 (BL-158) — extra columns become series, extra grouped rows merge into one line. FOUR columns, not five: NAME_VALUES.inoreader_call also lists 'oauth-refresh', which is the one category carrying zone1='0' and is therefore excluded by this panel's own blob7 = '1' filter. Giving it a column would plot a permanently-zero series, which reads as 'refreshes stopped' rather than 'never counted here'.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob2 = 'cron-radar')           AS cron_radar,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob2 = 'live-radar')           AS live_radar,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob2 = 'http-radar-snapshot')  AS http_radar_snapshot,
       sumIf(_sample_interval, blob2 = '401-retry')            AS retry_401
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'inoreader_call' AND blob7 = '1' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Inoreader calls by category, outcome and status
panels.description: status_code '0' isolates network-side failures from Inoreader-side ones.

targets.query:
SELECT blob2 AS category, blob4 AS outcome, blob6 AS status_code, sum(_sample_interval) AS calls
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'inoreader_call' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2, blob4, blob6
ORDER BY calls DESC

panels.title: What this dashboard deliberately does not show

options.content:
Four of the fourteen event types declared in `mcp-server/src/metrics/_schema.ts` **emit nothing in production**. A panel over any of them would render an empty chart that reads as *good news* — "no throttling", "all healthy" — rather than *no data*. So they are absent on purpose, and a guard test (`mcp-server/tests/unit/observability/grafana-dashboard.test.ts`) fails if one is added back.

The last two rows are omitted for DIFFERENT reasons and are **not** guarded: `audit_batch` and `cron_outcome` both emit, so a panel over either would be honest, merely redundant. Read the guard as covering the four types that emit nothing, not the whole table.

| Not shown | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Health checks** (`health_check`) | Declared in the schema, never emitted. `/status` health comes from live probes (`buildHealthPayload`), not from AE. |
| **Prompt spans** (`prompt_span`) | Emitter exists (`metrics/prompt-span.ts`); nothing calls it. |
| **IRL counters** (`wrong_irl_detected`, `gate_elided`) | Emitters exist (`metrics/irl-ingestion-events.ts`); nothing calls them. |
| **Audit batches** (`audit_batch`) | Emitted, but the pipeline is deactivated (ADR-0014), so counters legitimately read 0. |
| **Cron outcomes** (`cron_outcome`) | Genuinely live — omitted because `/status` and the seven alert rules already cover cron health. Add a panel here if that stops being true. |

**Why the refusal panels have no `allow` series**: `rate_limit_decision` is emitted **only on refusal**. An `allow` event would fire on every authenticated request — a volume class nothing else here occupies — and more rows means Cloudflare samples this dataset sooner. `count(DISTINCT blob8)` has no sample correction, so that would quietly degrade *Distinct active trials* in exchange for a number recoverable anyway (attempts ≈ invocations + denies). The trade and its rejected alternatives: [ADR-0032](https://github.com/reidperyam/gst-website/blob/master/src/docs/adr/0032-rate-limit-decisions-emit-only-on-refusal.md).

**Expected empty is not the same as broken.** The trial went live 2026-09-08, so its signup panels carry real data. The tier-gate and scope-denial panels can legitimately read zero — nobody hit the paywall or a scope wall in the window. What is NOT legitimate is a panel that reads zero because it queries a field its event types never write: that shipped three times (BL-158, BL-159) and is now caught by a guard binding panel SQL to `FIELD_EMITTED_BY`.

**Reading the numbers**: every count is `sum(_sample_interval)`, not `count()`, because AE samples. `count(DISTINCT x)` is a different aggregate from that corrected row counter and has no such correction — see the caveat on the *Distinct active trials* panel and [ADR-0031](https://github.com/reidperyam/gst-website/blob/master/src/docs/adr/0031-per-client-analytics-identity-is-a-blob.md).
